# New-ZbxProxyGroup

## SYNOPSIS

Creates a proxy group.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxProxyGroup [[-Name] <string>] [-FailoverDelay <string>] [-MinOnline <string>] [-Description <string>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A proxy group shares its hosts among its proxies and moves them to another proxy of the group when one goes offline (Zabbix 7.0 and later). The New-ZbxProxyGroup cmdlet sends proxygroup.create with one request field per parameter, then reads the new proxy group back with proxygroup.get and writes it. The server requires -Name; -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name and wins over a parameter. -WhatIf shows what would be created, and the command needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Create a proxy group

```powershell
New-ZbxProxyGroup -Name 'proxy-group-01' -FailoverDelay '1m' -MinOnline '1'
```

Creates a proxy group named proxy-group-01. The command writes the new proxy group, read back from the server.

### -FailoverDelay

How long a proxy in the group may go without contacting the server before it counts as offline, from 10s to 15m; time suffixes and user macros are allowed. Defaults to 1m.

| --- | --- |
| Type | `string` |
| Parameter sets | (All) |

| Position | Named |
| Default value | None |
| Pipeline input | True (ByPropertyName) |
| Wildcards | False |

### -MinOnline

Minimum number of online proxies, from 1 to 1000, needed for the group to stay online; user macros are allowed. Defaults to 1.
